properties.description: These papers collectively characterize the structure of LoRA weight space: asymmetry (B vs A), adaptive rank allocation (SVD), multiplicative adaptation (mLoRA), generative models (CVAE, hyper-convolutional). Together they inform the choice of weight-space coordinate system for WeightBench.
properties.relevance_to_research: Component 3 of WeightBench: choosing the right LoRA representation

properties.description: DEEP-ALIGN, GMNs, and DWSNets all address the fundamental challenge of permutation symmetry in weight spaces. DEEP-ALIGN learns equivariant alignment; GMNs use graph automorphisms; DWSNets use equivariant linear layers. These are the primary tools for symmetry-aware weight-space analysis.
properties.relevance_to_research: Critical for Experiment 2 (cross-model comparison) in WeightBench where weight-space distances must be symmetry-aware

properties.description: Task Arithmetic defines task vectors and simple merging; TIES-Merging adds sign election to resolve interference; DEEP-ALIGN adds equivariant alignment before merging. Together they form a progression of increasingly sophisticated merging methods. WeightBench could use merging compatibility as downstream prediction target.

SANE (sequential autoencoder) and GMNs (graph-based) both enable cross-architecture model comparison. The survey provides the taxonomy. Together they address the hardest open question in WeightBench: cross-model methodology for Experiment 2.
properties.relevance_to_research: Key tools for Experiment 2 (cross-model setting) in WeightBench

properties.description: DnD (hyper-convolutional) and ICM-LoRA (CVAE) both generate LoRA parameters conditioned on task descriptions without per-task fine-tuning. Both show that task descriptions and LoRA parameters are meaningfully linked in a learnable latent space.
properties.relevance_to_research: Could be used to synthesize LoRA populations for WeightBench experiments; demonstrate that behavioral signal (task description) predicts weight-space coordinates

properties.description: Weight disentanglement (Task Arithmetic paper) shows weight space has task-localized structure. ICM-LoRA's t-SNE shows task clustering in LoRA hidden space. mLoRA paper shows semantic structure in constrained LoRA weights. Together these support the WeightBench hypothesis that weight-space and behavioral coordinates are complementary, not redundant.
properties.relevance_to_research: Core theoretical motivation for WeightBench dual-signal framing

nodes.label: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
nodes.author: Gabriel Ilharco, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Mitchell Wortsman, Suchin Gururangan, Ludwig Schmidt, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Ali Farhadi

nodes.label: Task Vector
nodes.rationale: A task vector is obtained by subtracting pre-trained model weights from fine-tuned model weights, defining a direction in weight space. Arithmetic operations (negation, addition, analogy composition) on task vectors steer model behavior without extra inference cost, because operations are purely element-wise on weights.

nodes.label: Task Arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Negating a task vector unlearns a task; adding vectors creates multi-task models; forming analogies transfers knowledge to unseen tasks. Chosen because it requires no additional data or training and has zero inference latency overhead.

nodes.label: Weight Interpolation
nodes.rationale: Prior work on weight interpolation motivated the task vector construction. Linear interpolation between model weights can maintain or improve performance, underpinning the additive structure exploited by task arithmetic.

nodes.label: Weights2Weights: Interpreting the Weight Space of Customized Diffusion Models
nodes.author: Amil Dravid, Yossi Gandelsman, Kuan-Chieh Wang, Alexei A. Efros, Rameen Abdal, Gordon Wetzstein, Kfir Aberman
nodes.norm_label: weights2weights: interpreting the weight space of customized diffusion models

nodes.label: weights2weights (w2w) Space
nodes.rationale: A PCA-derived subspace over 60k+ LoRA fine-tuned diffusion model weights, one model per identity, functions as a meta-latent space. Sampling from it yields new identity-encoding models; linear directions correspond to semantic edits. LoRA is used to reduce dimensionality before PCA, making the manifold tractable.

nodes.label: Meta-Latent Space over Model Weights
nodes.rationale: Unlike GAN latent spaces that control individual images, the w2w meta-latent space controls the model itself, enabling consistent multi-image generation for a subject. This motivates treating model weights as data points in a learnable generative space.

nodes.label: ORAL: Prompting Your Large-Scale LoRAs via Conditional Recurrent Diffusion
nodes.author: Rana Muhammad Shahroz Khan, Pingzhi Li, Kai Wang, Dongwen Tang, Tianlong Chen
nodes.norm_label: oral: prompting your large-scale loras via conditional recurrent diffusion

nodes.label: Conditional Recurrent Diffusion for LoRA Generation
nodes.rationale: ORAL uses a recurrent diffusion backbone (from RPG) augmented with a novel conditioning mechanism encoding model architecture and textual task specifications. This achieves simultaneous scalability (up to 7B parameter LLMs), controllability (task-specific generation), and portability (transfer to evolving base models without retraining) — properties no prior method achieved together.
nodes.norm_label: conditional recurrent diffusion for lora generation

nodes.label: Neural Network Parameter Generation
nodes.rationale: Parameter generation treats neural network weights as a distinct modality to synthesize directly, offering an alternative to traditional training. Prior work (P-Diff, Cond P-Diff, RPG) each solved only a subset of scalability/controllability/portability.

nodes.label: Knowledge Is a Region in Weight Space for Finetuned Language Models
nodes.author: Almog Gueta, Elad Venezian, Colin Raffel, Noam Slonim, Yoav Katz, Leshem Choshen
nodes.norm_label: knowledge is a region in weight space for finetuned language models

nodes.label: Knowledge Region in Weight Space
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuned models optimized for high performance cluster in well-defined, linearly connected regions of weight space. Any model within a region also performs well. The center of such a region outperforms individual fine-tuned models on average, suggesting the best models may not lie at region edges (where gradient-based fine-tuning typically ends).

nodes.label: Linear Mode Connectivity
nodes.rationale: Models fine-tuned on the same dataset are linearly connected in weight space — the convex hull between them forms a connected low-loss basin. This extends the linear connectivity result of Entezari et al. to a full bounded convex region, not just a line.

nodes.label: Equivariant Deep Weight Space Alignment (Deep-Align / DWSNets)
nodes.author: Aviv Navon, Aviv Shamsian, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik, Nadav Dym, Haggai Maron
nodes.norm_label: equivariant deep weight space alignment (deep-align / dwsnets)

nodes.label: Deep-Align Framework
nodes.rationale: A learning-based weight alignment method using DWSNets with Siamese architecture. Alignment is reduced to a feedforward pass rather than iterative optimization (NP-hard in general). Equivariance design reduces training set size requirements and enables efficient inference.

nodes.label: Permutation Symmetry of Neural Networks
nodes.rationale: Deep networks maintain function under permutations of weights, making naive weight averaging or distance computation meaningless without alignment. This symmetry motivates equivariant architectures that respect it by design.

nodes.label: Weight Alignment
nodes.rationale: Finding optimal permutations between two networks' weight matrices to make them comparable. Critical for model merging, loss landscape study, and federated learning. NP-hard in general; prior work uses relaxed optimization.

nodes.label: Predicting Trends in the Quality of State-of-the-Art Neural Networks without Access to Training or Testing Data
nodes.author: Charles H. Martin, Tongsu Peng, Michael W. Mahoney
nodes.norm_label: predicting trends in the quality of state-of-the-art neural networks without access to training or testing data

nodes.label: Power Law (Heavy-Tailed) Metrics for Model Quality
nodes.rationale: PL-based metrics (weighted alpha, alpha-norm) derived from eigenvalue power-law fits outperform norm-based metrics for predicting model quality without training/test data. They can distinguish well-trained vs. poorly-trained models where norms fail (Scale Collapse). Based on Theory of Heavy-Tailed Self Regularization.
nodes.norm_label: power law (heavy-tailed) metrics for model quality

nodes.label: WeightWatcher Tool
nodes.rationale: A publicly available tool (v0.2.7) used to compute norm- and PL-based weight matrix metrics on pretrained models without access to training data.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
nodes.author: Armen Aghajanyan, Luke Zettlemoyer, Sonal Gupta
nodes.norm_label: intrinsic dimensionality explains the effectiveness of language model fine-tuning

nodes.label: Intrinsic Dimension of Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: The minimum number of parameters needed to achieve ~90% of full fine-tuning performance. Pre-training implicitly minimizes this intrinsic dimension, and larger models tend to have lower intrinsic dimension, directly motivating low-rank adaptation approaches like LoRA. RoBERTa can be fine-tuned with only 200 parameters projected back to full space.

nodes.label: Structure-Aware Intrinsic Dimension (SAID)
nodes.rationale: An extension of intrinsic dimension measurement that incorporates layer-wise scaling parameters. Addresses the limitation of layer-unaware DID by allowing different layers to contribute differently to the subspace optimization, reflecting that attention layers specialize separately.

nodes.label: LoRAGen: Structure-Aware Weight Space Learning for LoRA Generation
nodes.author: Hao Huang, Jingtao Ding, Mengqi Liao, Xin Wang, Jinyang Ban, Yuan Yuan, Huaiyu Wan, Yong Li
nodes.norm_label: loragen: structure-aware weight space learning for lora generation

nodes.label: LoRAGen Method
nodes.rationale: Generates LoRA parameters from natural language task descriptions using a latent diffusion model. Addresses non-uniqueness of low-rank decomposition by supervising on full adaptation matrix (not A/B matrices directly). Uses a module-aware Mix-of-Experts decoder to handle heterogeneous weight distributions across Transformer modules.

nodes.label: Non-Uniqueness of Low-Rank Decomposition
nodes.rationale: For any invertible R, (BR)(R^{-1}A) yields the same full adaptation matrix ΔW. Supervising on A,B directly is sensitive to arbitrary rescalings/rotations; supervising on ΔW avoids this ambiguity and improves generalization.

nodes.label: Module-Aware Mix-of-Experts (MoE) Decoder
nodes.rationale: Different Transformer modules (encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention, cross-attention) have systematically different spectral-entropy distributions. A shared decoder cannot model this heterogeneity; routing to module-specialized experts with structural embeddings addresses it.

nodes.label: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT (ROME)
nodes.author: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov
nodes.norm_label: locating and editing factual associations in gpt (rome)

nodes.label: Rank-One Model Editing (ROME)
nodes.rationale: Modifies feed-forward weights at specific middle-layer MLP modules to update factual associations. Uses causal mediation analysis to locate decisive neuron activations. Achieves specificity and generalization simultaneously, unlike fine-tuning or interpretability-based alternatives.

nodes.label: Causal Mediation Analysis for Knowledge Localization
nodes.rationale: Identifies which internal hidden states causally mediate factual predictions by corrupting subject tokens and restoring activations layer by layer. Reveals that middle-layer MLP modules at subject-last-token positions are decisive, not attention layers.
nodes.norm_label: causal mediation analysis for knowledge localization

nodes.label: Mid-Layer MLP Modules as Factual Association Storage
nodes.rationale: Factual associations in GPT are stored in localized, directly-editable computations within mid-layer feed-forward modules, not distributed across all layers, enabling targeted weight edits.
nodes.norm_label: mid-layer mlp modules as factual association storage

nodes.label: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
nodes.author: Edward Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Yuanzhi Li, Shean Wang, Lu Wang, Weizhu Chen
nodes.norm_label: lora: low-rank adaptation of large language models

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.rationale: Freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices (ΔW=BA) into Transformer layers. Motivated by the low intrinsic dimension of fine-tuning (Aghajanyan et al., 2020; Li et al., 2018). Reduces trainable parameters by ~10,000x vs GPT-3 full fine-tuning with no inference latency since ΔW can be merged at deploy time.

nodes.label: Rank Deficiency in Weight Updates
nodes.rationale: The hypothesis that weight changes during adaptation have low intrinsic rank justifies LoRA. Even rank r=1 or r=2 suffices for GPT-3 adaptation (d=12288), confirming the low-rank structure of adaptation deltas.

nodes.label: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
nodes.author: Dan Biderman, Jacob Portes, Jose Javier Gonzalez Ortiz, Mansheej Paul, Philip Greengard, Connor Jennings, Daniel King, Sam Havens, Vitaliy Chiley, Jonathan Frankle, Cody Blakeney, John P. Cunningham
nodes.norm_label: lora learns less and forgets less

nodes.label: LoRA Learning-Forgetting Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning in continued pretraining but forgets less of source domain capabilities. The constrained low-rank update acts as an implicit regularizer stronger than dropout or weight decay. Full fine-tuning produces high-rank perturbations (10-100x typical LoRA rank), explaining the performance gap in challenging domains like code and math.

nodes.label: High-Rank Weight Perturbations in Full Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: SVD analysis reveals full fine-tuning produces perturbations with rank 10-100x higher than typical LoRA configurations, challenging the low-rank hypothesis that motivated LoRA in difficult domains like code/math while barely changing the spectrum of base weight matrices.
nodes.norm_label: high-rank weight perturbations in full fine-tuning

nodes.label: Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Neural Network Weights for Model Characteristic Prediction
nodes.author: Konstantin Schürholt, Dimche Kostadinov, Damian Borth
nodes.norm_label: self-supervised representation learning on neural network weights for model characteristic prediction

nodes.label: Hyper-Representations of Neural Network Weights
nodes.rationale: SSL (reconstruction + contrastive) applied to populations of trained NNs (model zoos) to learn task-agnostic latent representations. Domain-specific augmentations (permutation, erasing, noise) are critical; permutation augmentation exploits weight-space symmetries and creates near-free valid NN samples for contrastive pairs.

nodes.label: Model Zoo
nodes.rationale: A dataset of trained neural networks with diverse configurations (data, hyperparameters, architecture). Serves as the training corpus for learning hyper-representations. Seed variation within a model zoo adds beneficial diversity for recovering model properties.

nodes.label: Permutation Augmentation for Neural Network Weights
nodes.rationale: Permuting incoming/outgoing weights of a neuron preserves the network's mapping exactly. This creates valid augmented samples at near-zero cost (each layer with N neurons has N! permutations) and exploits structural symmetry as an inductive bias for contrastive learning.
nodes.norm_label: permutation augmentation for neural network weights

Together they inform the choice of weight-space coordinate system for WeightBench.
properties.relevance_to_research: Component 3 of WeightBench: choosing the right LoRA representation

properties.description: DEEP-ALIGN, GMNs, and DWSNets all address the fundamental challenge of permutation symmetry in weight spaces. DEEP-ALIGN learns equivariant alignment; GMNs use graph automorphisms; DWSNets use equivariant linear layers. These are the primary tools for symmetry-aware weight-space analysis.
properties.relevance_to_research: Critical for Experiment 2 (cross-model comparison) in WeightBench where weight-space distances must be symmetry-aware

properties.description: Task Arithmetic defines task vectors and simple merging; TIES-Merging adds sign election to resolve interference; DEEP-ALIGN adds equivariant alignment before merging. Together they form a progression of increasingly sophisticated merging methods. WeightBench could use merging compatibility as downstream prediction target.

SANE (sequential autoencoder) and GMNs (graph-based) both enable cross-architecture model comparison. The survey provides the taxonomy. Together they address the hardest open question in WeightBench: cross-model methodology for Experiment 2.
properties.relevance_to_research: Key tools for Experiment 2 (cross-model setting) in WeightBench

properties.description: DnD (hyper-convolutional) and ICM-LoRA (CVAE) both generate LoRA parameters conditioned on task descriptions without per-task fine-tuning. Both show that task descriptions and LoRA parameters are meaningfully linked in a learnable latent space.
properties.relevance_to_research: Could be used to synthesize LoRA populations for WeightBench experiments; demonstrate that behavioral signal (task description) predicts weight-space coordinates

properties.description: Weight disentanglement (Task Arithmetic paper) shows weight space has task-localized structure. ICM-LoRA's t-SNE shows task clustering in LoRA hidden space. mLoRA paper shows semantic structure in constrained LoRA weights. Together these support the WeightBench hypothesis that weight-space and behavioral coordinates are complementary, not redundant.
properties.relevance_to_research: Core theoretical motivation for WeightBench dual-signal framing
